title: Multi-candidate generate/critique/repair loop with deterministic Python selection
hypothesis: A generate -> critique -> critique-the-critique -> repair -> deterministic verification loop can improve candidate coverage over single-answer rule-first prompting by broadening the proposal distribution while Python remains the judge.
primary_variable: Multi-candidate proposal/critique/repair loop instead of a single candidate answer.
split: permitted public ARC-AGI-2 training data only

generation_contract.cache_policy: CachedTargetClient fingerprint includes provider/model/full prompt/settings/solver/task/attempt; identical calls must reuse cache.

python_verifier.authority: Only deterministic Python execution and scoring count as evidence; critique text and model confidence never enter ranking.

success_threshold: At least 8 parseable non-duplicate candidates and either at least one exact training-consistent candidate for 06df4c85 or a dominant mechanically observed failure class supporting exactly one next ablation.
falsification: If candidate diversity is achieved but Python scoring yields neither an exact candidate nor meaningful near-miss/failure-cluster improvement, reject this loop variant and evolve exactly one component rather than repeating it unchanged.
leakage_policy: Public evaluation remains sealed; workflow sparse-checks out public training only and asserts evaluation is absent.
